newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Rate on Yugo cen.bank bonds hits new record high.
newsitem.headline: Rate on Yugo cen.bank bonds hits new record high.

text.p: The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) set a record high interest rate for its short-term bonds auctioned on Monday, raising it to an annual 147.48 percent, the Belgrade bourse reported.
This compares to the 121.80 percent interest rate set for the previous tranche of bonds auctioned on January 6. The lowest rate for those bonds was an annual 60.7 percent.
The NBY auctioned a new 20 million dinar ($3.84 million) tranche of its 30-day bonds and sold 10 million dinars worth, the bourse said.

Analysts said the NBY was trying to activate bonds as an instrument for regulating money supply, after substantial monetary expansion during the last few days of 1996 which sent the dinar plunging to 4.3 to the German mark during the eight-day New Year and Christmas holiday.
The central bank said late on Friday it would take decisive steps to stabilise the dinar and restore financial discipline.
But considering the size of the latest issue of NBY bonds, traders said the higher interest rate signalled the bank's key discount rate, set at 4.5 percent for January, will rise next month.

"The size of the issue is not large enough to sop up surplus liquidity created over the past week or so. Instead, the bank used the issue to create manoeuvring space to act with interest rates," one trader told Reuters.
The trader said the weighted interest rate for January stood at around 4.5 percent -- equivalent to the NBY's discount rate.
"The latest tranche of bonds, offered at 8 percent per month, inevitably leads to higher weighted interest rates for February, and this will reflect on the discount rate as well."
Traders also saw the latest NBY move as a prelude to an even tighter monetary stance. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
